# core/scan.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/scan.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Cutting a byte string into pieces: at white space, at
a separator string, or once at the first separator byte (`key=value`).
Every piece is a span of the string, so nothing is copied.

What is proved: every span returned lies inside the string (or inside the
span asked about), no word holds white space, no word is empty, and the
two halves of a `scan_split_once` lie on either side of a separator byte
that is really there. Not proved: that a separator string is found
wherever it occurs (see `bytes_find`).

`import "core/scan.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`scan_words`](#scan_words) | The words of `b`. |
| [`scan_split_str`](#scan_split_str) | The pieces of `b` between occurrences of the string `sep`, found from the left and not overlapping, in order. |
| [`scan_split_once`](#scan_split_once) | Cuts the span `s` of `b` at its first `sep` byte. |
| [`scan_count_byte`](#scan_count_byte) | How many bytes of the span `s` of `b` equal `c`. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `SpanPair`

```bastio
struct SpanPair { left: Span, right: Span }
```

The two parts of a string cut at a separator.

## Functions

### `scan_words`

```bastio
fn scan_words(b: &Bytes) -> Vec[Span]
  ensures words_ok(result, b)
```

The words of `b`: the maximal runs of bytes that are not white space
(`is_space`), in order. A string with only white space has none.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("  ls -l\t/tmp \n");
let ws = scan_words(b);
let mut ok = vec_len(ws) == 3;
if ok {
  let a = vec_get(ws, 0);
  let c = vec_get(ws, 2);
  ok = bytes_span_eq_str(b, a.start, a.end, "ls") && bytes_span_eq_str(b, c.start, c.end, "/tmp");
}
vec_free(ws);
let blank = bfrom(" \n ");
let none = scan_words(blank);
let empty = vec_len(none) == 0;
vec_free(none);
bfree(blank);
bfree(b);
if !ok || !empty { return 1; }
```

### `scan_split_str`

```bastio
fn scan_split_str(b: &Bytes, sep: &Bytes) -> Vec[Span]
  requires blen(sep) > 0
  ensures vlen(result) >= 1
  ensures forall i: u64 :: i < vlen(result) ==> span_in(vget(result, i), b)
```

The pieces of `b` between occurrences of the string `sep`, found from the
left and not overlapping, in order. There is one more piece than there
are separators, so an empty `b` gives one empty span.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("a::b:::c");
let sep = bfrom("::");
let parts = scan_split_str(b, sep);
let mut ok = vec_len(parts) == 3;
if ok {
  let x = vec_get(parts, 1);
  let y = vec_get(parts, 2);
  ok = bytes_span_eq_str(b, x.start, x.end, "b") && bytes_span_eq_str(b, y.start, y.end, ":c");
}
vec_free(parts);
bfree(sep);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `scan_split_once`

```bastio
fn scan_split_once(b: &Bytes, s: Span, sep: u8) -> Option[SpanPair]
  requires span_in(s, b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> span_in(result.Some.left, b) && span_in(result.Some.right, b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.left.start == s.start && result.Some.right.end == s.end
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.left.end < result.Some.right.start
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> bget(b, result.Some.left.end) == sep && result.Some.left.end + 1 == result.Some.right.start
```

Cuts the span `s` of `b` at its first `sep` byte: `key=value`, `host:port`.
`None` if the span has no `sep`.

Example:

```bastio
let line = bfrom("name = bastio");
let all = Span { start: 0, end: blen(line) };
let mut ok = false;
match scan_split_once(line, all, 61) {   // '='
  Option::Some(p) => {
    let k = bytes_trim(line, p.left);
    let v = bytes_trim(line, p.right);
    ok = bytes_span_eq_str(line, k.start, k.end, "name") && bytes_span_eq_str(line, v.start, v.end, "bastio");
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
let none = scan_split_once(line, all, 35);   // no '#'
let missing = none is Option::None;
bfree(line);
if !ok || !missing { return 1; }
```

### `scan_count_byte`

```bastio
fn scan_count_byte(b: &Bytes, s: Span, c: u8) -> u64
  requires span_in(s, b)
  ensures result <= s.end - s.start
```

How many bytes of the span `s` of `b` equal `c`.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("a,b,,c");
let n = scan_count_byte(b, Span { start: 0, end: blen(b) }, 44);
assert n <= 6;
bfree(b);
if n != 3 { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `words_ok`

```bastio
spec fn words_ok(v: &Vec[Span], b: &Bytes) -> bool {
  forall i: u64 :: i < vlen(v) ==> span_in(vget(v, i), b) && vget(v, i).start < vget(v, i).end
    && (forall k: u64 :: vget(v, i).start <= k && k < vget(v, i).end ==> !is_space_spec(bget(b, k)))
}
```

Every span in `v` lies inside `b`, is not empty and holds no white space.
